value.body: Designs the electronic circuits and printed circuit boards (PCBs) inside products — choosing components, drawing schematics, laying out boards and testing prototypes. Employers include electronics product companies, defence and aerospace electronics firms, automotive suppliers and engineering-services companies. A day mixes schematic and layout work, bench testing with lab instruments and fixing issues found in prototypes.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: PCB design software (schematic and layout), SPICE simulation, oscilloscope

items.label: Design areas
items.value: Power supplies, analog and digital circuits, high-speed boards

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join as trainee or graduate engineers in electronics product or engineering-services firms, through campus placement or direct applications; defence PSUs also recruit through their own notifications. A self-designed PCB project, taken from schematic to an assembled working board, and solid analog and digital fundamentals help at interviews.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: PCB layout and design for manufacture

value.title: At a glance
items: Openings are concentrated in a few electronics and engineering-services hubs.
Growth path: design engineer → senior → hardware lead or architect, or a move into RF or power electronics.
Design errors mean costly board re-spins, so careful review is a big part of the work.
